pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – SHORT STORIES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why are short stories important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition
2. use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition
   In simple words: practise until you can identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction
   In simple words: practise until you can use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories.
4. Show that you can: identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Work collaboratively with peers to conduct a reader’s theatre to read short stories on the theme (causes of road crashes and mitigation measures),
2. Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by finding the meaning of the vocabulary spelt.
3. Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner shows concerted attention to manage tasks when conducting a spelling bee contest to spell the vocabulary identified. Values:
4. Respect: It is promoted as the learner accommodates diverse opinions when sharing constructed sentences on vocabulary for peer review.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are short stories important?
2. Why is it important to ensure safety in your environment and especially roads?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition
2. use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
